scope: Mocked HTTP/Compose fault-injection lifecycle through real acceptance verifier; no live container run
semantics: Record stop intent before sending command
Only restore owned worker/scheduler stops, whose prior running state passed preflight
Verify observed running state after normal and exit-path starts
Attempt scheduler restoration even if worker restoration fails
Preserve original failure, partial checks and each restoration result
Restoration success does not make failed experiment pass
limitations: Docker unavailable, so actual service restoration is unverified
Running container state is not Celery readiness or business completion
Forced termination, host crash or power loss can bypass cleanup
Full-stack restart failures and externally changed service state are not covered by owned-stop recovery
